name: Compliant Stablecoin (bridge-in)
tagline: USDC bridged in, then paid privately bank-to-bank — the Issuer gates KYC but sees no amounts
concept: A regulated stablecoin brought onto the consortium ledger and transacted privately. Real USDC is locked in a bridge vault on the public chain (a transparent, public event); against it the Issuer mints a 1:1 representation onto the permissioned ledger as a KYC-gated ZK token. From then on payments are zero-knowledge: only the owning bank can value its notes. The Issuer is the compliance anchor — it controls issuance/redemption and the KYC allowlist (so an un-admitted party simply can't transact) — yet it sees neither amounts nor who-pays-whom. That's compliance without surveillance: admission control at the edge, privacy in the middle. Other consortium members and the public see only ZK commitments and nullifiers.

steps.title: Bridge in: lock public USDC, Issuer onboards the banks
steps.plain: Real USDC is locked in a bridge vault on the public chain — a transparent, public event. On the consortium ledger the Issuer deploys a KYC-gated ZK stablecoin and admits Bank A and Bank B. An un-admitted party can't transact: its transfer proof would fail.

steps.title: Bridge mint: Issuer mints 1,000,000 to Bank A
steps.plain: Against the locked USDC, the Issuer mints the representation 1:1 to Bank A. The Issuer sees the issuance it performs (the edge) — but from here the value is a ZK note only Bank A can decrypt: the Issuer cannot read Bank A's balance, nor any payment Bank A later makes (the middle).
steps.tech: coin.mint({ to: bankA, amount: 1000000 })  ·  ZK commitment on-chain

steps.title: Private payment: Bank A pays 250,000 to Bank B
steps.plain: Bank A pays Bank B. The ZK proof shows both are KYC-registered and value is conserved — without revealing the amount or the parties. Only Bank A and Bank B see their own notes; the Issuer, other members and the public see only a nullifier + commitment.
steps.tech: coin.transfer({ to: bankB, amount: 250000 })  ·  nullifier + ZK commitment
